processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five different alloys synthesized in one operation using five movable Cu molds filled successively from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³ blocks hot rolled into 2±0.1 mm thick and ~500-mm-long sheets.
Parent homogenization treatment (proc_homog-1100c-2h-wq) applied to all RAP samples before aging.
Defining heat treatment of this sample: after homogenization, aged in air at 600 °C for 24 h, then oil quenched.

structures.overall_structure: Austenitic microstructure; for Al content below 5 wt.% a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature. Base state after hot rolling and water quenching is fully recrystallized with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained Mn microsegregations.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

yield_strength.uncertainty: approximate range read from Fig. 3a for the 4Al composition region

ultimate_tensile_strength.uncertainty: approximate range read from Fig. 4 for the 4Al point cluster

elongation.uncertainty: approximate range read from Fig. 4 for the 4Al point cluster

hardness.uncertainty: approximate value read from Fig. 3d for the 0-6Al region

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: aging sensitivity of mechanical properties (YS, UTS, TE, hardness)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 4Al sample: YS ~350-450 MPa, UTS ~460-600 MPa, TE ~8-55% (Fig. 3/Fig. 4).
Hardness ~200 HBW for the 4Al composition (flat region 0-6Al in Fig. 3d).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; as-cast coarse dendritic microstructure; hot-rolled + WQ state fully recrystallized with ~20 µm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al is an intermediate Al variant: alloys with 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% Al are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments (450/500/550/600 °C, 0/1/24 h) in terms of mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening).

For the intermediate Al variants with 2–6 wt.% Al (including 4Al), a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior is observed; pronounced strengthening during aging is attributed mainly to nm-sized κ-carbides in the ~8 wt.% Al variant.

For Al content below 5 wt.%, a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature; for 25–30 wt.% Mn with up to 4–5 wt.% Al (when naturally aged) the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism (SIMPLEX steels).

κ-carbides (L′1₂ structure, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC) have a lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to an austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix and can form cuboidal nanoprecipitates; they are thermally very stable at 600 °C and prevail after 100 h heat treatment with only modest coarsening (general κ-carbide statements, not specifically quantified for the 4Al sample).
